scaling_axes: Size: h, the homecoming multiplier, applied per homecoming. It compounds over time and is the dominant axis. The Golden Egg multiplier (once per Bird) and the golden homecoming multiplier (tail) also sit here. Redbreast and the Cuckoo pay a share of each landing Bird, so they grow with size too. Applications: homecomings per Bird. Trips, Mrs Stork's step and recalls, Old Tern and Mrs Dunnock drive them. The missed-fight rule caps them hard at one per 2 rounds, so this axis saturates, which is why the Stork dials move little. Count: how many Birds grow per homecoming. The Cuckoo share times the Birds in play drives it, plus the number of fliers cycling, which the roster and stayer slots fix rather than a dial. Additive feeders the size axis multiplies: Chiffchaff's gain, Supper and Jack Daw's steal. Time: each Bird compounds by h every 2–3 rounds. In trivariate terms Birds have about one and a half axes: size times time, count only through the Cuckoo, and applications capped. B raises size (h 2.25) and count (Cuckoo 1/8). C raises all three: h 2.5, Cuckoo 1/5 and Stork every 5 gold, plus the Golden Egg at x3.

counting_convention:
This follows the harness convention (HARNESS.md "Metrics"; fight_capture.gd combat_start). The figure is each Fairy seat's pre-start, end-of-recruit board for round 12: after that round's End of Turn effects and before any Start of Combat trigger. It is Attack + Health summed over every unit standing on the board, including its slot's Ring stats, rounded as built at ceil(count x Ring size) per stat per slot. Shy units (Hob, Lob, Silky) count their body only, because Shy ignores slot stats.

Excluded:
- Cradle Fetch's copy. Fetch counts only as its own 2/4 body plus its own slot's Ring, because the copy is made at Start of Combat (pass3_fairy_combat.gd runs after the combat_start snapshot).
- Wisps, which are summoned at Start of Combat.
- Rings on empty slots.
- Witch, Changeling, Belladonna, Hob and Reel effects.

Fairies have no Eggs. Hand, away, doorstep and Belly reserves are empty in these scripts, so they add nothing.

"Typical" is the median of 8 equally weighted scripted lines: ring full, ring slow, ring mid (slow, no Silky), ring low (no Lob or Silky), court full, court slow, court mid (no Silky) and court with no tier 6. The harness's committed table has both line_fairies_engine and line_fairies_tempo seats, which is why the ensemble takes both lines. The high roll (golden Cluricaun on R8) and the top 1% are reported separately as tails. A post-start figure (adding the Fetch twin at fetch_share, plus Wisps) is given beside each number, but it is not the checkpoint number.

counting_convention:
What the R12 figure counts: a Bog seat's PRE-START, end-of-recruit board. That is the printed plus permanent Attack + Health of every unit on its 7 slots. It is measured after this turn's Start of Turn gains have landed (pending Soak from the last fight, Tiddy's and Nan's Toll shares) and after any frog doubling in the last fight.

Not counted:
- Peatlings (summoned mid-fight).
- Bitter's shrink on enemies.
- The Toll itself (a number, not stats).
- Anything in hand, such as a held His Highness.
- Fight-only effects: Jenny's pull, the Lantern's lure, Sal's fire, Hopkin's borrowed Attack, Gideon's hit back.

Bog has no Eggs, Bellies, away or doorstep units, so active stats = board stats, and nothing is reported as reserve.

"Typical" means the median of 9 timing variants of the synthesis's typical court line: the frog bought at R8, R9 or R10, times Tiddy at R7, R8 or R9. This smooths the frog's ×2 jumps the way a lobby median would. A single line's R12 point swings ±15%.

Bog is parasitic, so the enemy board is the preset's own field:
- B: the Sep 2025 shape ramped to 900 at R12 (R6 53, R8 130, R10 342, R12 900, R14 2,076).
- C: ramped to 1,800 (R6 53, R8 164, R10 542, R12 1,800, R14 4,153).

The field at fight time is assumed equal to its pre-start size.

Bog scales on size and time. Count and applications are held at design.

- **Count** (how many buffs and sources): the number of Soak drinkers and patches (Toad, Gideon, Jenny, Lantern and King 1 each, the Prima Donna 3, the Chorus lends 2). - **Applications** (how often each fires): every bite on a patch (about 1.4-1.5 a fight per patch, set by the enemy's attackers and Mire). Soak, Tiddy and Nan pay every turn. The frog fires every 3rd kiss (bog_kiss_period 3; one kiss a fight is a guard). All held.
- **Size** (each application): bog_bitter_share (1/4, held) x the biter's Attack x bog_soak_keep.

  - The Toll's size dials are bog_nan_share (1/2 in B and C) and bog_tiddy_share (1/2, held). Ranocchio's own size dial is bog_ranocchio_share (1/2).
  - The frog's x2 is a multiplicative size step on two units, held.

scaling_axes:
Hunters scale on size × count × applications. Time works against them. They don't compound on themselves; they compound only through the field and through winning more.
- Size comes from the prey. Every gain is a fraction of an enemy unit's stats at the bell, so the field supplies this axis. The Hunter dials set only the fraction: Takers (Nip, Sable, Lutra), the Glutton, the Lodger, Wick, Grizel and the Pelt. B and C move only these.
- Count is receivers per kill. The Taker gains, the Glutton gains on every Take, the Lodger on Takes beside him, and every pack attacker under Grizel (Wick on his joins). The board's makeup sets the count; the Glutton, Lodger and Grizel shares set what each extra receiver gets.
- Applications are Takes per fight, about 2.6–3.0 and nearly flat with standing. They come from structure: Quarry, Isegrim's gang, Old Brock's and Lutra's reach, and Brother Wolf and Agnes keeping leaders alive. Two dials multiply them: the Laird ×2 on 'Take:' text and Ermeline's one Pelt a fight, which doesn't need a win. Neither is raised.
- Time is the one-round lag (gains land next Start of Turn, reading last round's prey) plus how steep the field is. With design dials, Hunters reach 0.99× a ×1.5 field, 0.69× the B field and 0.40× the C field. That is why B and C need raises even though the shares already scale with the field. The pieces come online at the Glutton (R9–R10) and the Laird and Isegrim (R11), which is why the boards run 1.3× the field by R14.
